extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Speech data was collected by having three different native speakers record each of 2009 sentences from the FLoRes-101 dataset (dev and devtest sets) in 102 languages. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponded to the input sentence, with invalid recordings discarded. A balance in sex ratio of at least 30/70% was imposed when possible. All recordings were kept as-is from either quiet or noisy environments without data augmentations. The speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of sentences from the FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia that have been translated into 101 languages by human translators. The dev and devtest sets (2009 sentences total) were used as the source material for speech recordings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each sentence in 102 languages, three recordings were collected by three different native speakers with a balance in sex ratio of at least 30/70% when possible. After recording, each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated in the first version of the dataset.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings per sentence, with between zero and three recordings retained after validation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers with a balance in sex ratio of at least 30/70% when possible
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset shows performance disparities across geographical groups, with Western European languages achieving better results (10.7 CER) compared to Sub-Saharan African (15.6 CER) and South Asian languages (17.4 CER), partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data available for Western European languages from existing datasets like MLS and VoxPopuli.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. Languages unseen during pre-training generally achieve worse than average CER due to fine-tuning on very limited supervised data. The dataset maintains recordings as-is from quiet or noisy environments without data augmentations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding. The dataset aims to reduce gaps across geographical groups and advance massively multilingual speech and text representations.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes recordings from native speakers with imposed balance in sex ratio of at least 30/70% when possible. Speakers are different between train and dev/test sets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval. The dataset is well-suited for downstream tasks including ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available via TFDS and Huggingface. Future versions are planned to fill gaps where recordings are missing (about 21.5% of sentences in the first version).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For textual data, NFC and FST normalization is applied to each sentence, followed by lower-casing, normalization and punctuation removal. Words are split into characters with token 'j' as word boundaries. Three versions are provided: original raw transcript (SRC_RAW), preprocessed version (SRC_NORM), and character-based version (SRC_CHAR) for ASR. All recordings are kept as-is from quiet or noisy environments without any data augmentations (e.g., SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation). Speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
